How does your OBD2 adapter connect?
Most adapters. The app finds yours, and pairs it if needed.
No adapters found. Is the ignition on?
Join the adapter\'s Wi-Fi network first.
Type the 17 characters from your VIN plate or registration papers. It\'s kept on this phone only, and used for your car\'s make, year and reports instead of the VIN the car sends.
A VIN is 17 letters and numbers, without I, O or Q.
Make and year appear after connecting.
Automatic (recommended)\nTries every protocol, starting with the one that worked last time
Leave on Automatic unless your car won\'t connect.
If your car won\'t connect, choose it so the app tries its usual protocol first.
The app tries this car\'s usual protocol first, and waits longer for it.
Start typing, e.g. Corolla, CX-5 or Civic. Leave blank if it\'s not listed.
If this doesn\'t work, the app still tries every other protocol.
Drive for about half a minute to get a score.
Connect to score this drive. Scores are worked out on your phone and never saved.
Racing is for track days and closed roads only.
So the app can explain your car\'s own fault codes, set the rev dial to its redline and find its protocol faster. You can change it later under Diagnostics.
Optional. Tap to see the engines offered that year, or type your own.
Electric: there\'s no engine to choose.
Optional. Type your engine, e.g. 2.0 or 3.0 V6.
Pick how your dash looks. Your choice is saved.
Connecting an adapter, choosing your car and Android Auto

1. Plug your ELM327 adapter into the car's OBD2 port, usually under the dashboard near the steering wheel.
2. Turn the ignition on (the engine can be off).
3. Tap Connect and choose how your adapter connects.

No adapter? Tap Demo to try the app with a simulated car.

Bluetooth: tap Connect, then Bluetooth. The app lists your adapter by name, whatever kind of Bluetooth it uses. If it needs pairing, Android asks for a PIN: it\'s usually 1234 or 0000.\n\nWi-Fi: join the adapter\'s Wi-Fi network in your phone\'s settings first, then connect. The usual address is 192.168.0.10, port 35000.

Check the ignition is on and the adapter\'s light is lit. Then, on the Diagnostics tab, tap Your car and choose your car\'s make, year and model, so the app tries its usual protocol first. Older cars may not fully support OBD2 (it became required from 1996 in the US, 2001 in Europe, about 2006 in Australia and later in many other countries), and some cheap adapters can\'t talk to older Fords, GM and Chrysler cars.

Android Auto only shows apps from the Play Store until you allow others. To turn that on:
1. Open Android Auto's settings on your phone (search "Android Auto" in Settings).
2. Scroll to the bottom and tap Version about 10 times, then confirm to turn on developer mode.
3. Tap the three-dot menu at the top right, then Developer settings, and turn on Unknown sources.
4. Reconnect to your car. OBD2 Reader appears in Android Auto's app list.

Connect to your adapter from the phone first, or tap Connect on the car screen to reconnect to the last one.

OBD2 Reader reads the trouble codes the engine computer, and on many cars the automatic transmission, report through the OBD2 port. On CAN cars, Diagnostics → Codes from other modules also reads codes from modules such as ABS, power steering and the instrument cluster, at the addresses your make uses. Airbag modules are never asked. The app never clears codes; that needs the maker\'s tool or a scanner made for your make.\n\nNearly all generic codes (P0, P2, P34, U0 and U3) are explained, with causes and what to check. The few that aren\'t are named by the system they belong to. Manufacturer-specific codes (such as P1 codes) are marked as such, with where to look them up for your make, because their meaning differs between brands. A few Ford and Lincoln codes use Ford\'s own definitions, for the model years Ford\'s documents cover.

Beside the battery voltage, the app shows whether the battery looks like it's charging. Standard OBD2 has no battery-current (amps) reading, so this is an estimate from the voltage and engine speed, marked (est.).

Engine running: 13.2 V or more is charging; 12.8 to 13.2 V is charging weakly (normal on cars with smart charging, which lower the voltage while cruising); under 12.8 V is not charging; over 15.2 V is overcharging. Engine off: under 12.2 V means the battery is low.

Scan what your car reports, on this tab, shows whether your car offers any battery readings of its own.

Your location is never sent to the developer or anyone else. It\'s only saved when you record a drive and choose Save route, and then only on your phone, in that drive\'s CSV file. The app only uses it to draw the outline of your route on the drive\'s share card, and the card shows just that outline: no map, street names or coordinates. Delete the drive and its route goes with it. Positions come from your phone\'s own location service, the same one maps apps use, so your phone\'s Location settings apply as usual.

OBD2 Reader only reads from your car. It never clears trouble codes, turns off the check-engine light or changes any setting, and it blocks any command that could. After a repair, a workshop scan tool can clear the codes.
Readings your car reports, with their value now. Tap one to add or remove its graph; up to %1$d at once.
Up to %1$d graphs at once, so each one stays fast
Recording is off. Tap Record drive to save every reading to a CSV file on this phone, which you can open in Excel or Google Sheets, and the route too if you choose.

The app can save where you drove with this recording, so you can map it in other software and see its outline on your drive card. Your location goes only into this drive\'s file on your phone, and only while it records. It\'s never sent to the developer or anyone else, and the app only uses it to draw your route\'s outline on the share card. You can delete the drive any time.
Reconnects to your adapter when you open the app, start Android Auto or turn the ignition back on.
What may not work with this car
Drive for at least half a minute to get a score.
Watch the battery while the car is off

Leave the phone connected to the adapter overnight (on charge, in range) and the app notes the battery\'s voltage every 5 minutes, then says whether it held its charge or something may be draining it. The adapter uses a little power itself, so don\'t leave it plugged in for weeks. Without this, the app stops waiting for the car after 30 minutes.
Checked each time the engine starts while the app is connected: connect with the ignition on and the engine off, then start the engine. A healthy battery stays above about 10 V while starting.
Tap a drive for its summary and to share its card. Tap and hold to delete it from the history (a recording of it stays in Saved drives).
It\'s removed from Drive history. If you recorded it, the recording stays under Graphs → Saved drives.
You can also tap and hold a graph, then drag it up or down.

Sound and vibrate if the engine runs hot or the battery stops charging. The codes are checked every 30 seconds while you drive, and a new one arrives as a quiet notification. Shown on Android Auto too.
For closed roads and track days only. Timed from your car\'s speed readings, so older cars that report speed less often are less precise.
Connect to your car (or the demo car) first.
Choose what the Dashboard\'s main readouts show, for example intake air instead of fuel.
Lists every reading your car offers, including ones the app doesn\'t show yet, and tries known manufacturer readings. Share the result to help add support for your car.
A used-car check: how far the car has gone, and how many times it has warmed up, since its trouble codes were last cleared.
The engine computer\'s own emission checks: which have finished since the codes were last cleared. Also shows its software version.
The measurements behind those checks (oxygen sensors, catalyst, misfires and more), with the limits each must stay within.
Reads codes from modules beyond the engine, like ABS, transmission and power steering. Read-only: nothing is cleared, and airbag modules are never asked.
Asks every address a module could use, for modules the app doesn\'t know your make has. Takes about a minute, and only reads.

Fords and Mazdas put the cluster, body, climate, audio and door modules on a second, slower network (pins 3 and 11). Adapters that can switch to it, such as OBDLink MX+ and EX, can read those too. Takes about a minute, only reads, and never asks the airbag module.
Readings your car\'s maker added beyond standard OBD2, like transmission temperature and oil life, live, plus each module\'s part numbers and software versions.
These readings come from owners testing them on their own cars, not from the maker, so check one against your car before relying on it.
Hybrids and electric cars: the high-voltage battery\'s charge, plus how fast it\'s charging, with a graph.
Your car didn\'t report a high-voltage battery. Petrol and diesel cars don\'t have one, and some hybrids and EVs keep it to their maker\'s own tools.
Watching the charge. Its pace shows after about 3 minutes.
Keep this open while the car charges (or drives) to see the pace. The car reports its charge in small steps, so the pace settles after a few minutes.
Charging needs the battery\'s charge, which your car didn\'t report.
Readings marked Unofficial come from owners testing them on their own cars, not from the maker, so check one against your car before relying on it.
Read-only: the app only reads what the car reports. It never wakes, switches or commands the high-voltage system.
Live speed, coolant and battery while connected; otherwise your last battery reading, code check and drive. Connect or disconnect from the home screen.
Off to start with. Once on, while you\'re connected, leaving the app keeps your readings in a small floating window over your other apps, like a video. Drag it anywhere; tap it for controls.
The colour of the app\'s icon on your home screen and in the app list.
Add a reading by its request and formula, for ones the app doesn\'t list yet.
No custom readings yet. Add one with its request (service 01, 21 or 22), an optional module address and a formula using A, B, C… for the reply bytes.
Requests are read-only: only services 01, 21 and 22 are allowed. Touch and hold a reading to delete it.
The ¼ mile is an estimate: distance is worked out from your car\'s speed readings, not measured by timing beams like a drag strip.

To install updates, Android needs you to allow OBD2 Reader to install apps. Turn on Allow from this source, then come back and tap Update again. You only need to do this once.
This is a test build, signed differently from the released app, so updates can\'t install over it. Open the release page to get the released app instead.

Tap to see what\'s new and update.

You can also download the new version from the release page and open it to install. Your settings, drives and recordings are kept.
Android didn\'t respond after the update was downloaded, so it wasn\'t installed. The phone may have blocked it without saying so.
On Samsung phones, Auto Blocker stops apps installing updates. Turn it off under Settings › Security and privacy › Auto Blocker, tap Update again, then turn it back on if you like.
Record drives from the Dashboard once you\'re connected. Recorded drives are kept here under Saved drives, to share or make a video overlay from.
Something not working? Tell me on GitHub. Your app version and phone are filled in for you.
An idea for a new feature, or for making something better.
How much of your VIN the app shows on screen and puts in code reports, car scans and adapter logs you share. The last 6 characters are your car\'s serial number: the part that says which car it is.
Permanent codes: %1$s. The engine computer keeps these until its own test shows the fault is fixed, which can take a few drives after a repair. No scan tool can clear them.
Every trouble code seen on your car, with when it first showed and when it went
No trouble codes seen yet. Each time the app reads your car\'s codes, any it finds are added here, kept on your phone only.
Codes the app has seen on each car, kept on your phone only. Ones that have gone are greyed.
This clears the app\'s list on your phone. It doesn\'t change anything in your car: its codes stay as they are.
Show one style by day and another by night. The switch fades over gently, and waits while you\'re using the screen.
This phone has no light sensor, so \"With the light around the phone\" goes by sunset and sunrise instead.

Sunset and sunrise are worked out on your phone from the date, the time and roughly where you are: the phone\'s last known location if you\'ve let the app use location, or else your time zone. Your location is never saved or sent anywhere.
Android Auto goes by your car\'s own day and night (its light sensor or headlights), with the same day and night styles. Widgets follow the phone\'s style.
Worked out from your time zone, so it can be up to an hour out. Once the app may use location (it asks when you record a drive\'s route), it\'s exact.
The phone\'s dark theme is on.
The phone\'s dark theme is off.
Keep a copy of your settings and drives, or move them to a new phone

A backup is one file with your settings, chosen car, styles, reading choices, custom readings, alert settings, drive history, code history and recorded drives. Keep it somewhere safe, like Google Drive, a computer or a USB stick, and restore it on a new phone.
Routes of recorded drives (where you drove)

The file stays wherever you put it: the app doesn\'t send it anywhere. Anyone who has the file can open it and see what\'s in it, including your routes (and so where you live or work) if you leave them in.
Disconnect from the car first, then restore.
Left out: %1$d settings this version doesn\'t use
Restoring replaces this phone\'s settings with the backup\'s. Drive history, code history and recorded drives are added to what\'s already on this phone: nothing on it is deleted.
Drive off and brake once in a straight line
From the phone\'s motion sensor. Harsh moments are shown here and don\'t change the scores.
Replay a saved recording, or turn on recording to save your car\'s replies.
Recording is on: each connection\'s replies are saved on this phone.

Saves what your car answers to each request the app makes (the app only ever reads), in a plain text file on this phone. Replay it later to see the app work without the car, or share it with a bug report. Your VIN is left out unless Hide VIN is set to show it in full. The newest 10 recordings are kept, up to about half an hour each.
Recording starts the next time you connect.
No recordings yet. Turn on Record car replies, then connect to your car.
It\'s removed from this phone. Copies you saved or shared stay where they are.
This recording can\'t be read, so it can\'t be replayed.
Disconnect first, then replay the recording.
